In brief
- Hollywood studios and production companies are warning employees not to bet on prediction markets using insider knowledge, The Hollywood Reporter reported.
- The rules bar bets on casting, release dates and earnings, and at least one company has set up an anonymous hotline to report colleagues.
- A Columbia law professor said bets on blockchain-based platforms can be "basically impossible" to trace if insiders hide their identities well.
Hollywood studios and production companies have been quietly issuing guidelines barring employees from betting on prediction markets, entertainment industry trade paper The Hollywood Reporter reported on Thursday.
The warnings prohibit staff from betting on events such as studio earnings, casting decisions and release dates, or passing information to friends and family so they can bet instead, according to the report. At least one company has reportedly set up a hotline for employees to anonymously report colleagues suspected of placing bets.
The Hollywood Reporter's own parent company, Penske Media, has also updated its employee handbook in recent weeks to ban bets on "award nominations, casting decisions, production timelines and release dates," the outlet said.
#1 Searched TV Show on Google 2026?
The rules extend long-standing bans on insider trading in the stock market to platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket, which let users bet on everything from who will be cast as the next James Bond to who will be voted off a reality show.
"You now have, essentially, an explosion in the number of employers who have to think about insider trading rules from an ethical standpoint," Joshua Mitts, a law professor at Columbia University who studies prediction markets, told the outlet.
Enforcing those rules may be another matter. "With blockchain-based trading, it can be basically impossible if you know how to use a mixer correctly and know how to hide your identity behind multiple layers of intermediation," Mitts said.
Some bookmakers are already spooked. Betting site BetOnline temporarily pulled its market on the next James Bond this week after a sudden wave of "sharp money" pushed actor Callum Turner above longtime favorite Jack Lowden, raising concerns about a leak, according to the report.
Who will be the top Spotify artist of 2026?
Insider trading on prediction markets
Entertainment insiders have been caught before. In February, Kalshi said a video editor at MrBeast's company had made about $5,000 using confidential information to bet on MrBeast content; he was fired and fined $20,000.
Federal prosecutors have also brought cases over insider trading on prediction markets. In April, an active-duty U.S. soldier was charged with using classified information about the raid to capture Nicolás Maduro to bet on Polymarket. In May, a Google engineer was charged with commodities fraud, wire fraud and money laundering over Polymarket bets allegedly placed using confidential company data. Both cases are pending.
Governments have moved too. California, New York and Illinois have banned state employees from using nonpublic information to bet on prediction markets, while the platforms have rolled out their own surveillance tools. Polymarket has investigated dozens of bets on the U.S. midterm elections.
One kind of entertainment bet is already off the table. Under the Onion Futures Act of 1958, U.S. law explicitly bans just two types of futures contracts: those on onions and those on movie box office receipts, The Hollywood Reporter noted.

In brief
- Solana Labs’ Leap launched a beta mobile app for trading tokenized stocks, ETFs, metals, currencies and crypto, available in early access on iPhone.
- The app curates market-moving news on price charts and tracks detailed profit and loss, with trades routed through Jupiter.
- Leap charges no fees at launch but plans to use future fees to buy and burn SOL and fund a referral program.
Solana Labs is betting the network’s next wave of traders wants more than meme coins.
Leap, a new company under Solana Labs, launched a beta of its mobile trading app Thursday, letting users trade tokenized stocks, ETFs, metals, currencies, and crypto in one place, around the clock and subject to restrictions.
The app is available in early access on iPhone through Apple’s public TestFlight program, with an Android version coming soon. It isn’t available in the U.K. or other restricted regions.
SOL next move: Pump to $160 or Dump to $40?
Leap is built by the team behind Dialect, which Solana Labs acquired earlier this year. Dialect developed Solana Actions and Blinks, a protocol that turns blockchain transactions into shareable links, which launched in 2024, as well as the cashtags feature on X.
The company is pitching the app as an alternative to fast-paced meme coin trading, aimed at people who want to make better-informed decisions over the long term. Its research team curates market-moving news and pins each story to the price chart at the moment it broke.
The app tracks profit and loss across every deposit, withdrawal, trade and fee, including each position’s breakeven price. Users enter an amount in dollars, and each trade executes as an onchain swap.
Leap uses Jupiter for trade routing, Helius for infrastructure and Birdeye for market data.
“The Solana blockchain now confirms a trade in about 150 milliseconds thanks to Alpenglow, so the network is now faster than ever,” said Chris Osborn, Leap’s general manager and Dialect’s founder. Alpenglow a consensus overhaul designed to sharply cut Solana’s confirmation times.
“Every app that brings new people onchain makes the whole ecosystem stronger,” said Solana Labs co-founder and CEO Anatoly Yakovenko.
Leap isn’t charging its own fees at launch, though network and routing costs apply. It plans to use future fees to buy and burn SOL, permanently removing tokens from circulation, and to fund a referral program. Early waitlist members, dubbed the Founders Club, would earn 30% of the trading fees generated by users they invite and 5% from those users’ own referrals.
Leap arrives as tokenized stocks gain traction on Solana and beyond. Securitize has brought tokenized Nvidia, Apple, and Amazon shares to Solana. The trend has also met pushback: 56 companies have objected to having their shares traded on OKX and ICE’s planned tokenized stock venue.

items.author: Cointelegraph by William Suberg
items.content:
Bitcoin crashes 6% to 7-week low as US stocks erase election gains
Bitcoin saw sudden downside at the Wall Street open as stocks witnessed a snap sell-off, reversing post-election gains.
Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $76,000 on Thursday as risk assets abruptly reversed their US midterm elections rally.
Key points:
- Bitcoin fell to $75,463 its lowest levels since Sept. 16, amid a worsening stock sell-off.
- Risk assets gave back gains from the US midterm elections, with the Nasdaq Composite Index dropping 4.2%.
- BTC/USD briefly fell below its 50-week simple moving average (SMA), at $75,733, putting the level’s role as support under pressure.
BTC price sinks below $76,000 amid risk-asset rout
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD shedding more than 6% to $75,463 on Bitstamp, its lowest levels since Sept. 16.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
After making swift gains on the back of a Democrat sweep of the US House of Representatives and Senate, equities saw sharp selling on Thursday as traders rotated out of tech. The S&P 500 fell 2.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index lost more than 4% to hit its lowest levels since July 29.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Oil rebounded amid reports of fresh strikes on tankers in the Middle East and uncertainty over what steps Democrats may take to resolve the US-Iran war. WTI crude returned above $90 per barrel, while Brent gained 2.5% to approach $97.
CFDs on WTI crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
“We may be headed for more volatility as investors digest the election results and potential policy implications,” Jordan Watson, a portfolio manager at Tandem Investment Advisors, told CNBC. Watson added that equities gains following the midterm results should not be treated as an “all-clear signal.”
Previously, Cointelegraph reported on concerns that Democrat policies could be less favorable to the AI sector, potentially curbing already precarious capital expenditure plans.
Economist Mohamed El-Erian questioned whether the change in US political trajectory would really have a long-term negative impact on the tech sector. “Will the shift in Congress actually slow tech down? If yes (as many assume, though I’m less sure), can the rest of the market and economy thrive without the shield of tech earnings and spending?” he wrote in a blog post.
El-Erian described the day’s tech-stock weakness as “not surprising.”
Related: Bitcoin win rate vs. S&P 500 recovers as post-midterm history favors stocks
Bitcoin 50-week trend line support at risk
Crypto markets liquidated nearly $500 million in positioning in the first hour of the US trading session, per data from CoinGlass, with 24-hour total liquidations nearing $850 million at the time of writing.
BTC/USD vs. crypto liquidations. Source: CoinGlass
Now targeting $76,000, BTC/USD approached the bottom of its one-month trading range. The pair risked losing support at the 50-week simple moving average (SMA), currently at $75,733.
BTC/USD one-day chart with 50-week SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
In his latest analysis, crypto trader Rekt Capital noted that Bitcoin was repeating behavior from May, when a period of rangebound moves around $80,000 subsequently gave way to a breakdown and new macro lows of $57,000 in late June.
BTC/USD three-day chart. Source: Rekt Capital

There are plans to expand the Crypto Investor Consumer Bill of Rights—a Clarity Act amendment led by Dem. Maxine Waters—into a broader market structure bill, journalist Eleanor Terrett tweeted. 🚨SCOOP: House Democrats are discussing plans to expand the Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights, @RepMaxineWaters’ amendment to the Clarity Act in 2025, into a broader crypto “market structure” bill next Congress.
The proposal would fold in Democratic Clarity Act…
— Eleanor Terrett (@EleanorTerrett) November 4, 2026
On the surface, the midterm election results could be seen as a major hit to crypto policy in the U.S., with President Trump's Republican administration widely regarded as the pro-crypto party, while the Democrats were deemed more hostile. However, experts, told Decrypt, the tide might be turning and crypto policy evolving into a more bipartisan issue.
Crypto candidates and the Clarity Act
Advocacy organization Stand With Crypto endorsed 45 candidates in the midterms, per its election tracker, with 27 pro-crypto candidate wins, 12 losses, and six races still live at the time of writing. Nearly half of the endorsed candidates were Democrats.
"We’re proud to see a majority of our endorsed candidates win their elections," Mason Lynaugh, executive director of Stand With Crypto, said in a statement shared with Decrypt. "To the candidates who won’t return to Washington, thank you for going to bat for crypto-owning Americans when it counted."
Congratulations to the pro-crypto champions who won their elections, including more than 50 pro-crypto new members heading to Congress.
In the closest races, our advocates showed up: in Florida's 9th District, Darren Soto won by 1,477 votes. In that same district, we mobilized… pic.twitter.com/lcq055GNET
— Stand With Crypto🛡️ (@standwithcrypto) November 4, 2026
James Butterfill, head of research at CoinShares, described Republican Bryan Steil as a "meaningful loss" for crypto. The Wisconsin Congressman was the chair of the House digital assets subcommittee and closely involved in efforts to advance the Clarity Act—which were stymied when it stalled in the Senate earlier this year.
That said, Butterfill also highlighted several winners—Democrats Chris Pappas in New Hampshire and James Talarico in Texas, as well as Wyoming Republican Harriet Hageman—who have supported crypto policy. He stressed, however, that the challenge is now "converting" that support into passing legislation. Some believe that could slow an already difficult path for the Clarity Act.
"I wouldn’t say it’s game over for Clarity, but passing it has become tougher," Carlos Guzman, vice president of research at crypto trading firm GSR, told Decrypt. "Some Democrats support clearer crypto rules, but I wouldn’t expect it to be high on their agenda. Any agreement will likely require stronger provisions on things like consumer protection and conflicts of interest."
The Clarity Act looks to establish rules for crypto markets and has been batted back and forth since 2025. Democrats have pushed back on the bill, citing Trump's crypto conflicts of interest, with Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) pushing for the bill to ban officials and their families from profiting from the sector.
"For other crypto policies, the election doesn’t automatically replace the leadership of the SEC or CFTC or stop their rulemaking," Guzman said. "Congressional oversight does change, however, so we might see more scrutiny of regulatory decisions, with Democrats also able to influence agency funding and future appointments."
Butterfill added that he believes crypto is becoming less dependent on the Clarity Act, as the SEC and CFTC push for regulatory clarity without the need for Congress. He also said that AI regulation may take eyes away from crypto, slowing crypto policy in the process.
Following the midterms, Bitcoin has exhibited volatility, and is currently trading at around $76,820, down 4.1% on the day, per Decrypt data.
"The result alone would not make me change my medium-term Bitcoin outlook," Butterfill told Decrypt. "Slower reform could delay some institutional activity, but we would expect the more direct impact to fall on US crypto businesses reliant on new regulatory permissions. We would revisit the outlook if political uncertainty materially weakened investment flows or tightened financial conditions."

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin slid toward $76,000, erasing Wednesday's breakout, as roughly $428 million in crypto longs were liquidated within an hour.
- The Nasdaq approached correction territory as chipmakers and data-center firms fell on concerns over AI spending and Democratic oversight.
- Wednesday's rally included a massive short squeeze, with futures data pointing to repositioning rather than a comparable influx of new buyers.
Bitcoin erased Wednesday's post-election rebound Thursday as a technology stock selloff spread to cryptocurrencies, triggering hundreds of millions in forced liquidations.
Bitcoin fell to about $76,500, down nearly 5% and back near levels seen before Wednesday's jump above $80,000. Ethereum shed more than 5%, while other major tokens suffered comparable losses. Roughly 90% of the top 100 cryptocurrencies were in the red during the selloff, while roughly $428 million in crypto longs were liquidated in one hour.
Wall Street offered no shelter. The S&P 500 lost about 2.6% in late-morning trading, while the Nasdaq sank nearly 4%, approaching a correction, or a 10% drop from its peak.
The election is part of the answer, but anxiety over AI spending and interest rates is making the damage worse.
The election rally meets the AI selloff
Democrats' sweep of Congress initially rattled investors expecting tougher oversight of industries favored by President Donald Trump. Stocks rallied Wednesday as traders bet gridlock would limit major policy changes and falling oil prices would ease inflation. Bitwise Europe analyst André Dragosch also told Decrypt the Democratic sweep was "largely priced in."
Thursday brought a different interpretation. Investors weighed what Democratic control might mean for the data-center boom, particularly in states where voters oppose rising electricity costs and new facilities.
And the new political configuration is already moving things. Voters in at least 29 U.S. jurisdictions backed restrictions on data-center development, although not every measure is binding. UBS estimates potential pauses could threaten 30% of planned U.S. data-center capacity additions in 2028, per Reuters.
"We suspect there is going to be some scrutiny on this aggressive AI buildout," Swissquote senior analyst Ipek Ozkardeskaya told Reuters.
Chipmakers and AI infrastructure companies took the hit first. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped about 8%, while CoreWeave and Nebius fell by double digits. Tesla also tumbled roughly 9.5%, extending losses after Elon Musk spent heavily backing Republican candidates. Investors were also questioning the returns on massive AI investments.
The S&P 500 had the biggest bearish intraday movement in months, dropping almost 4% in minutes.
"The market's moving from the promise of AI to the price of AI," Ted Parkhill, chief executive of Incline Investment Management, told Reuters.
The political shift also threatens crypto's ambitions in Washington. Democratic control complicates efforts to revive the stalled Clarity Act, a proposed federal rulebook for digital assets. The new Congress will not take office until January. Politics alone cannot explain Bitcoin losing thousands of dollars in an hour.
Why Bitcoin's rebound fell apart
Wednesday's rally looked dramatic, but much of its buying pressure came from traders closing losing bets against Bitcoin. About $378 million in short positions were liquidated in one hour as Bitcoin pushed above $80,000, according to CoinGlass data.
Today’s reversal flipped the liquidation machinery in the opposite direction. Exchanges automatically close underfunded longs as prices fall, generating more selling and the enormous red candles visible on Bitcoin's hourly chart.
Crypto was already vulnerable before the election. The market had lost roughly $300 billion in value over the previous month, amid concerns about AI spending, rising borrowing costs and the fallout from last week's multibillion-dollar Binance hack.
Traders also expect another Federal Reserve rate increase in December as inflation persists. Friday's October jobs report could alter those bets; higher rates generally hurt demand for speculative investments.
Technically, Bitcoin's still-forming daily candle is threatening a bearish engulfing pattern, potentially swallowing Wednesday's green body and erasing the breakout in a single session.
The hourly chart shows selling through $79,000 to near $76,100. The next test is $75,000, while reclaiming $80,000 could ease the pressure—but Thursday's candle has not closed, so the pattern remains unconfirmed.

items.content:
--- Top Comments ---

[rhoohr]: > What is it like to hear vocal folds vibrate? I wouldn't normally describe hearing a voice as hearing "vibrations". Vibrations are indeed the physical basis of sound, and the auditory system detects changes in air pressure caused by them. But vibrations can also be perceived through touch, and the subjective experience of hearing is quite different from the tactile sensation of feeling something vibrate. When talking about feeling vibrations, I usually think of the touching...

[losvedir]: >  But I cannot know what sound is really like, because I have no memory of normal hearing.  and >  I was born with normal hearing. I began losing my hearing in childhood ... After I was registered, I started wearing hearing aids. People's voices became clear, and for a few months things were good. ... A specialist told me that I badly needed cochlear implant surgery, but I hesitated because it was very expensive.  I'm confused what's going on here.

[hackerci]: ENT surgeon who has bilateral CIs and has been in the research field for 20+ years. This sort of stuff is cool, but there are lots of limitations at the auditory nerve interface that limits improvements to speech and music processing strategies. Crazily enough, many of these studies were done in the 1960s to 1990s and are still valid today. There are strategies that can help at individual level, but do not help everyone. Thus they have not made it to clinical use.

[libpcap]: Software like Voicemod transforms speaking voice into a bright, robotic, or Miku-inspired digital idol tone in real time. I wonder if this would help in hearing and understanding speech better.

[cosmojg]: Their GitHub repo with all of their data is here:  https://github.com/mi-rae-lab/ci-psychophysics-data

items.content: ![image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/main/assets/reth-prod.png) ## Summary Reth v2.10.0 is a hardening release. It fixes an engine panic after a reorg below the persisted tip, bounds `eth_callBundle` work, and stops `reth download` from deleting files outside the datadir. It also brings several RPC correctness fixes and P2P interop fixes. `db repair-trie` now verifies storage in parallel, and `--tracing-otlp` can write spans straight to a local file. SDK users: the commit-condition callback on `BlockExecutor` and `BlockBuilder` now also receives the transaction's state changes (see Breaking Changes). ## Backwards Compatibility > [!IMPORTANT] > v2.10.0 can be downgraded to v2.9.0. ## Update Priority | User Class | Priority | |---|---| | Payload Builders | High | | Non-Payload Builders | High | ## Breaking Changes ### SDK - The commit-condition callback on `BlockExecutor` and `BlockBuilder` now also receives `evm2::TxStateChanges`, so payload builders can decide whether to keep a transaction based on its state changes as well as its result ([#28207](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28207)) ## Features ### Performance - `db repair-trie` verifies storage in parallel, with new `--storage-workers` (default: available CPUs) and `--storage-lookahead` (default: 1024) flags. A dry run now requires the node to be stopped ([#28078](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28078)) ### CLI - `--tracing-otlp` accepts `file:///absolute/path` and writes OTLP spans to a local file, with no collector needed ([#28215](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28215)) ## Bug Fixes ### Engine & Trie - Fixed an engine-thread panic when building an invalid-block witness after a reorg below the persisted tip ([#28249](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28249)) - Fixed the trie iterator's seek decision at cached branch boundaries ([#28264](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28264)) - Payload tasks keep their parent tracing spans ([#28221](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28221)) - Detached trie and overlay tasks keep their parent tracing spans ([#28259](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28259)) ### RPC - `eth_callBundle` now takes a blocking-IO permit, stops when the client disconnects, and shares one gas limit across the bundle ([#28253](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28253)) - Pending block builds stop when the request is cancelled ([#28251](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28251)) - Empty reverts return `0x` data ([#28243](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28243)) - `mev_simBundle` reports the refundable value before payouts ([#28218](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28218)) - `trace_replayBlockTransactions` returns an error for an unknown block ([#28160](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28160)) ### P2P - Extra fields in the p2p `Hello` message are ignored ([#28180](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28180)) - Extra fields in discv4 `ENRResponse` are ignored ([#28232](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28232)) - Trusted peer IDs are kept when their DNS lookup fails at startup ([#28202](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28202)) - Known peers are promoted when they're trusted by hostname ([#28199](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28199)) ### CLI - `reth download` rejects output paths that escape the datadir and skips cleanup through symlinked parent directories ([#28247](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28247)) - ERA index listing handles multibyte separators ([#28222](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28222)) ### SDK - The custom precompile example keeps its precompile after Prague ([#28237](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28237)) ## Dependencies - evm2 `592bf18` - alloy-* 2.5.0 - alloy-primitives 1.6.1 Full changelog: [v2.9.0...v2.10.0](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/compare/v2.9.0...v2.10.0) ## Binaries [See pre-built binaries documentation.](https://reth.rs/installation/binaries) The binaries are signed with the PGP key: `50FB 7CC5 5B2E 8AFA 59FE 03B7 AA5E D56A 7FBF 253E` ### Reth | System | Architecture | Binary | PGP Signature | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---| | | x86_64 | [reth-v2.10.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/releases/download/v2.10.0/reth-v2.10.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) | [PGP Signature](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/releases/download/v2.10.0/reth-v2.10.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz.asc) | | | aarch64 | [reth-v2.10.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/releases/download/v2.10.0/reth-v2.10.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) | [PGP Signature](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/releases/download/v2.10.0/reth-v2.10.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz.asc) | | | aarch64 | [reth-v2.10.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/releases/download/v2.10.0/reth-v2.10.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz) | [PGP Signature](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/releases/download/v2.10.0/reth-v2.10.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz.asc) | | | Docker | [paradigmxyz/reth](https://ghcr.io/paradigmxyz/reth) | - 纽约时报：美军数千名空军和海军人员待命，对伊朗军事行动计划已就绪

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 5 日，据《纽约时报》报道，尽管特朗普已暗示并不急于重启轰炸行动。但这种可能性依然存在：过去一些总统在突然陷入「后备选项」地位时，常常会动用军事手段，部分目的就是向外界表明其作为最高指挥官的权力并未削弱。2006 年布什在中期选举中历史性地落败后加快了在伊拉克的行动。一些长期在中东地区工作的前美国国务院外交官、五角大楼官员和军事指挥官表示，特朗普可能已经把自己逼入了绝境。

五角大楼官员和军方指挥官当地时间周三表示，数千名美军空军和海军人员，部署在十余艘舰艇及中东各地和美国境内的基地，已准备就绪，将根据特朗普的命令重新展开针对伊朗的大规模作战行动。相关官员透露，美以两国军队已制定出具体计划，实施一次短期但密集的军事行动，其目标很可能是伊朗的能源基础设施、核设施以及导弹和无人机武器库。

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
达里奥的另一面：患过睾丸癌、崇拜马斯克、认为成年人死亡损失是婴儿的3倍

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 曾经得过睾丸癌。2014 年，他确诊后接受化疗，最终完全康复。这段经历此前鲜为人知。11 月 5 日，《纽约时报》采访了 20 多位达里奥的朋友、同学和前同事，试图还原这位 AI 安全派代表人物的另一面。

达里奥对死亡和时间的关注，可以追溯到更早之前。2006 年，他的父亲因丙型肝炎去世，没能等到后来让大多数患者获得治愈机会的新药。达里奥原本研究物理学，此后逐渐转向生物学，希望通过新技术加快医学进步。朋友回忆，他曾坚持严格的游泳训练、尝试抗衰老补剂和限制热量摄入，经常谈论时间的有限性，认为时间是唯一无法再生的资源。

早在 2007 年，达里奥就迷上了 AI 超越人类智能的设想。他曾向朋友预测，技术奇点可能在 2040 年到来，人类甚至可能与机器融合。但他同时警告，如果 AI 没有被正确开发，人类可能就完了。

当时，他深受 AI 安全思想家 Eliezer Yudkowsky 和有效利他主义运动影响，还曾与马斯克通信。两位知情人士透露，达里奥年轻时很欣赏马斯克，甚至考虑过去他的公司工作，只是最终没有成行。

2010 年，达里奥在慈善机构 GiveWell 的博客中写道，成年人拥有比婴儿更丰富、更深刻的生活体验，因此他认为，一名成年人死亡造成的损失，可能是婴儿死亡的 2 至 3 倍。

当时他正比较两个慈善项目，一个致力于防治成人结核病，另一个帮助非洲儿童接种疫苗。按照他的生命价值判断，拯救成年人更有优势。但最终，他却将 1 万美元全部捐给了儿童疫苗项目。他更看重后者可靠的执行过程，以及奖励高效慈善机构可能带来的长期影响。

为了帮助更多人，他甚至考虑过放弃科研、转行金融。2010 年，他在一封邮件中表示，自己正在考虑从事金融工作，因为这样能赚到更多钱用于捐赠。

这种相信理性计算、重视执行可靠性的思维方式，也体现在他对 AI 的看法中。他认为超级 AI 可能毁灭人类，因此必须由真正重视安全、值得信任的人来开发。这种对 AI 安全的强烈信念，在 OpenAI 内部逐渐演变成了关于谁有权监督技术、谁能参与核心项目的争执。

2018 年，OpenAI 研究员 Joshua Achiam 反对由达里奥担任公司首席伦理官。他担心 Amodei 兄妹权力过于集中，主张引入外部专家，避免少数人垄断 AI 的伦理监督权。知情人士回忆，达里奥当面提高嗓门，坚称没有人比自己更适合这个职位。

围绕 GPT 项目，冲突更加激烈。达里奥与妹妹 Daniela 主导相关研究后，极力阻止 OpenAI 总裁 Greg Brockman 参与。达里奥多次向 Altman 下最后通牒：如果不能让 Brockman 远离项目，自己就会辞职。

Altman 最终拒绝让步。2020 年 12 月，达里奥兄妹与多名同事离开 OpenAI，四周后创办 Anthropic。这场决裂还掺杂着研究成果归属、管理权和长期积累的个人恩怨。达里奥认为 Altman 淡化了自己的贡献，也曾明确表示无法与 Brockman 共事。

颇具反差的是，2016 年特朗普首次当选美国总统后，达里奥曾在 OpenAI 内部消息中表达对美国政治走向的担忧。他认为，投资人 Peter Thiel 因支持特朗普而在道德上应受到谴责，OpenAI 不该继续接受他的钱。但后来，Thiel 创办的风险投资机构 Founders Fund 却成了 Anthropic 的投资者。

如今，达里奥领导的 Anthropic 正推动更严格的 AI 安全监督。他也因主张限制对华芯片出口、加强监管和警惕 AI 失控，与黄仁勋、扎克伯格等科技巨头发生公开分歧。支持者认为他在负责任地开发 AI，批评者则认为，他试图让少数公司掌握过多技术权力。

达里奥本人拒绝接受《纽约时报》的这次采访。

items.content:
--- Top Comments ---

[NewJazz]: musl’s crypt() returns the string * as an error indicator when the key is over 256 bytes long. * is also exactly what the stored field contains for every account with no password, so the “hash” matches and the login succeeds.  Does anyone know why musl does this? Are they the only C library that behaves this way? For a C library that famously tries to adhere to POSIX as much as possible, this seems like a crazy choice. From POSIX standard:  Upon successful completion, crypt() shall return a p...

[0127]: IMO this is where languages like Rust shine. The design patterns built into the language for handling errors (Result) - force you to handle errors / function results with sentinels, null pointers, or errnos are so much more error prone than handling a Result<T,E> using a match statement. crypt() returning `*` is insane especially since these kinds of sentinels are all over /etc/passwd

[feearent]: Not really related to the topic, but AI-popular sentences and language structure stand out to people right away these days right? I noticed some. "If you cannot update yet, at least disable password logins: set PasswordAuthentication no in your sshd configuration and restart sshd.  Either one closes the hole. " (only AI would characterize a critical SSH implementation vulnerability as a hole closing game) An attacker who can reach your SSH port can log in without knowing any passwor...

[throwa356262]: Discussion from a few hours ago:  https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50377221

[drob518]: Given Alpine’s broad use in the Docker ecosystem, this is going to hit a lot of folks, I think.

items.content:
--- Top Comments ---

[porphyra]: Servo is really great: Rust seems like a no brainer choice for a modern web engine, and its clean, performance-focused design from the ground up is wonderful. But it seems really hard for it to get anywhere just based on occasional contributions from volunteers. I was actually quite surprised that basic functionality like <progress> and the :checked attribute were not even supported prior to this release. Servo got 527 commits, while Chromium has over 20,000 commits.

[robin_reala]: Remember that if you value Servo you can sponsor them, details at  https://servo.org/sponsorship/

[shakna]: Progress got my attention. As an on-again off-again project, I've been building an incremental game that is pretty much just hundreds of progress bars - a little bit out of the norm for the browser. Firefox everything renders smoothly and gently. Chrome chugs, skips paints, delays animation frames, skips some events, and batches others. Game uses a few features that aren't in Servo yet... But maybe I can tweak it...

[ericyd]: It's heartening to see a large group of people working (mostly) for free on a passion project. Makes me optimistic about the resilience of intrinsic human drive.

[caminanteblanco]: One of the things I find really helpful about servo (as a casual user) is the breadth of pre-built releases they have. It makes it much more feasible to actually use on a day-to-day basis, especially on android

items.author: Jacob Lyon
items.content: Spooked US regulators are reportedly contacting banks to probe for unusual activity or disruptions in the wake of the $6.3 billion Binance hack. US banks are also trying to learn from the hack and are reportedly checking their own security systems to figure out if they’re prepared to respond to a similar hack. That’s according to various sources speaking to Reuters, which reports that officials from the Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency have been reaching out to banks to assess the impact of the Binance hack. Read more: LIVE: Binance says it’s yet to open up more token withdrawals One source whose bank was contacted said there weren’t any disruptions to their services, but that they’ve prepared statements for customer inquiries. Another claimed that AI’s rapid evolution has meant banks are having to commit even more resources to cybersecurity while struggling to keep up with hackers. Reuters also reported that a cybersecurity team at one of the largest US banks contacted Binance in the wake of the hack. Its goal is to create its own internal report that will review the bank’s security systems. Binance hack caused by malicious ad and fake job interview Binance was hacked on October 29 following a series of security breaches targeting three Binance employees. An engineer looking for a popular AI coding tool first clicked on a malicious search engine ad for a software installation program before downloading the malware-laden program. This security breach was detected and dealt with by Binance, but the details of the engineer and his team had already been leaked. Three months later, another Binance engineer was tricked into a fake job interview, which led to them downloading an “assignment” containing malicious code. This malware subsequently extracted sensitive information from the engineer, and by October 29, it was able to log into a third Binance engineer’s computer and launch the malicious script that caused the $6.3 billion hack. VerifiedX Ships Vault Update Aimed at Stopping Hacked vBTC Transfers

VerifiedX today released upgraded self-custodial recovery Vaults as part of its Mainnet 9.0.0 upgrade. Bitcoin holders using vBTC can set a delay before transfers from their vault become final, allowing them to recall mistaken or unauthorized transfers during that window and recover assets to an owner-designated self-custodial address. These protections are enforced on-chain by VerifiedX network consensus, without requiring a separate custodian. The upgrade also embeds Bitcoin light-client verification into VerifiedX’s validator software, enabling validators to independently verify Bitcoin block headers, proof of work and chain progression with 6 confirmation burial depth. — link

items.author: rwilinski
items.content:
--- Top Comments ---

[nater5000]: This is too dense. You might as well just post some Python code with sufficient comments to get the same point across. I think a nicely written article with a few diagrams would go a long way. Sometimes less is more. MCPs don't really need this level of technical explanations (it's basically just a REST API with standardized endpoints for discovery aimed at agents), and AI agents really do lack in the taste dimension when it comes to these things.

[Zaheer]: These vibe code explainers look nice on the surface but actually make things even more confusing. There's an element of curating which information to present and when that doesn't come across here.

[bluegatty]: MCP is an enterprise tool. Anything fleeting -> just use a skill. The advantage of MCP is thin, and it only starts to show when it's really well integrated, and your company platform provider does the integration. Otherwise it's a huge pain in the rear to keep your cli integrated with all the MCPs. MCP is good for things you use literally 'all of the time' - or - it's seamlessly integrated into your system and you don't have to think about it. Otherwise, just ...

[ndriscoll]: Are MCP calls composable in e.g. codex yet? e.g. can a model pipe a jira MCP call to grep or sed, or at least into a file? Last I looked at MCP it was just a vastly worse version of curl, .netrc, and some short text files describing calls (which are themselves greppable). Is there anything useful beyond that that I'm missing?

[dirteater_]: The interesting and necessary part of MCP is auth. A more useful explanation would cover a lot more of the "why", because looking at any thread mentioning MCP you'll see a ton of people saying "CLIs and traditional REST APIs do the same thing, why do we need yet another spec". Sure now there are apps and tasks in the spec to handle specific usecases, but those can also be DIY'ed without the protocol and agents can still use them.
items.title: MCP Explained

items.author: Jacob Lyon
items.content:
Binance has removed all of its API keys associated with crypto trading terminal SignalPlus as an “immediate precautionary measure” following a hack at the third-party firm.
Binance posted today to its X account, “Binance’s own systems are unaffected. User funds remain safe.”
Crypto derivatives exchange Deribit also removed all SignalPlus API keys in response to a potential incident.
Read more: BitMart hit by $391K hack amid security staff exodus
SignalPlus says $82K in user funds were stolen
SignalPlus has since confirmed on X that it was hacked and under $82,000 worth of user funds was stolen.
It claims it was targeted via a compromised Telegram account belonging to one of its third-party partners.
“Posing as this contact, the attacker communicated with one of our engineers and sent a fake Microsoft Teams meeting invitation,” SignalPlus claimed.
The engineers computer was comprised, and then, by November 4, the waiting hacker “began using the engineer’s access privileges to attack our internal network.”
SignalPlus says it was able to shut down the incident, and that it will reimburse user losses. In the meantime, SignalPlus’ services will remain unavailable until it’s confirmed everything is secure again.
Binance warned users to check their accounts and positions
Binance advised its users to review their positions and open orders while waiting for SignalPlus to give the all-clear before “rebinding any API keys, and always enabling IP whitelisting.”
The exchange also called for its third-party partners to “review their security controls, monitor for unusual activity and contact us immediately if they detect any concern.”
Crypto hack after crypto hack
Binance was hacked for $6.3 billion earlier this month and is currently in the process of opening up further withdrawals and replenishing the stolen funds.
Already this month, Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin was hacked, as was BitMart.
Read more: Crypto survived cybersecurity awareness month… just
SignalPlus is partnered with major crypto firms such as Bybit, Gate.io, and OKX.
Update November 5, 14:07 UTC: Updated this article to include SignalPlus’ hack disclosure.

items.content:
In brief
- OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said it was "fucking annoying" that his comments about computer memory were taken out of context, after Elon Musk mocked them.
- Altman had said it was "quite terrible" for the world's limited supply of DRAM to sit in home computers that are used 5% of the time.
- He briefly renamed himself "Ram Altman" on X, saying he wants people to be able to put as much memory in their computers as they want.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has hit back at criticism of his comments about computer memory, saying they were taken out of context and that he has long argued for the world to make more of it.
"I actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers, and it is fucking annoying that this was taken out of context," Altman tweeted early Wednesday. "I have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time."
but only because...i actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers, and it is fucking annoying that this was taken out of context.
i have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time.
— Sam Altman (@sama) November 4, 2026
The post came as Altman leaned into the backlash. Replying to users joking about his remarks, he said he "lol'd" at one meme and, when another asked him to rename his X account "Ram Altman," replied "ok yeah," briefly changing his display name before explaining he had only done so because he wanted people to have plenty of memory.
Altman's original comments came in an interview with YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, where he discussed shortages of memory and other components caused by the AI boom. "From like a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time," he said. "You want maximum utilization in a cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment."
In the same interview, Altman also blamed memory makers for being slow to expand production, and said he would be "very sad" if prices for chips and other components did not fall.
The remarks drew widespread criticism, including from Elon Musk, who mocked Altman on Sunday with a meme of the Inglourious Basterds character Hans Landa asking, "You are withholding DRAM from the cloud, are you not?" "The people deserve to have their RAM too!" Musk wrote.
The global RAM shortage
The spat comes amid a global memory shortage driven by demand from AI data centers. SK hynix, one of the world's largest memory makers, warned last week that demand for memory would outstrip supply through 2030.
Contract prices for 16GB DDR5 memory chips rose from $8.70 in October 2025 to $48 in September 2026, an increase of more than 550%, according to Tom's Hardware. On an earnings call this week, Chen Ching-wen, CEO of memory maker Team Group, said there was "no downward price trend whatsoever," and warned that some buyers could face a situation where "even money can't buy goods."
The crunch has already pushed up prices for consumer devices. In April, Meta raised the price of its Quest 3 and Quest 3S headsets by $50 to $100, weeks after Sony increased PlayStation 5 prices.

items.content:
Blockchain is ‘perfect solution’ for AI agent trust, VeChain CEO says
Sunny Lu said AI agents would need identity and reputation systems, making the case while promoting agent-building platform VeWorld.ai.
AI agents could drive blockchain’s next adoption cycle by creating demand for systems to verify their identities and reputations, according to VeChain co-founder and CEO Sunny Lu.
Autonomous AI agents operating around the clock would require a “new accountability system” to build public trust, Lu said during Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction show on Wednesday.
“The perfect solution is a blockchain,” he said.
Lu made the case while discussing VeWorld.ai, an agent-building platform that uses VeChain’s blockchain.
In his vision, agents would have digital “passports” and operate within a “decentralized credibility system” that tracks their reputations and those of their creators. Smart contracts could help settle transactions between agents or between agents and people.
VeChain has also pursued blockchain adoption through supply-chain tracking, including food traceability projects.
AI agents could help people monetize their expertise
AI agents could also help people turn their expertise into businesses or services, extending software-building opportunities to non-developers, according to Lu.
He compared the opportunity to mobile app stores, which allowed individual developers to distribute and monetize their work. Agent-building tools could open that market to people whose skills lie outside programming, including those with specialist professional experience, local knowledge or hobbies.
His own experiments included an educational agent for his daughter, an agent to support his mother’s daily routine and recovery, and a virtual employee to manage purchasing, inventory, sales and operations for an acquaintance’s shop in Milan.
Other industry participants have highlighted the risks of relying on agent providers.
In an October interview, Animoca Brands chairman Yat Siu told Cointelegraph that crypto traders could put AI agents to work around the clock but warned that users risked building their trading strategies around services they did not control.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Christina Comben
items.content:
Can decentralized phone networks power the AI revolution?
Decentralized AI networks want to turn everyday phones into an alternative to centralized computing infrastructure — but skeptics have their doubts.
The sprawling data centers that underpin the AI revolution have become about as popular as baby toys made from asbestos.
Campaigners around the world highlight the massive amounts of energy and water the infrastructure requires, while markets worry about the revenue required to pay back the $38 billion cost of building a single, one-gigawatt AI data center.
But is there another way to power the AI revolution that’s sitting in your pocket right now?
As of October 2026, there are an estimated 7.68 billion mobile connections worldwide, and billions of smartphones are currently lying unused in pockets, on desks and in drawers.
Each one has a processor, memory and an internet connection, and represent a vast pool of computing power just waiting to be put to work.
So could a network of humble smartphones realistically power AI at scale?
Putting smartphones to work
Decentralized AI networks are emerging that aim to turn everyday smartphones into a distributed infrastructure layer, and reduce reliance on costly, centralized data centers.
Acurast says it has onboarded more than 335,000 smartphones to its network. Co-founder Alessandro De Carli says that around 40,000 of those are fully active on an average day, providing computing capacity for tasks ranging from web scraping and cybersecurity to AI inference and agent hosting.
Data center locations across the US. Source: World Resources Institute
Related: DePIN grows into a $10B sector despite token slump, Messari says
He says smartphones are particularly efficient for certain workloads. Their built-in hardware security features “excel” in areas like confidential computing or an “isolated environment” that can install and run executables. They are also well suited to workloads that are “CPU intensive,” or which require wide distribution and “unfiltered access” to the internet,
“Servers are better at multi-threading, but smartphones offer unmatched compute efficiency,” De Carli tells Magazine.
While ordinary smartphones have limited memory, and big servers retain an advantage when handling multiple tasks in parallel, he says many workloads can still fit within the memory available.
Taken as a whole, the active phones on the network “match the compute capacity of about 2,340 high-end data-center servers,” he claims, benchmarked against the ASUS RS720A-E11, a high-density server built for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing (HPC).
Mobile connectivity in 2026. Source: Datareportal
Another project, Phase, launched Phase Proxy in October, which allows smartphone owners to provide internet connectivity and blockchain validation for AI agents. Founder Kirill Eves explains that, “websites routinely block or rate-limit automated traffic originating from data centers,” so the system employs users’ mobile and residential connections as a proxy instead. Phase plans to charge 0.5 USDT per 1,000 requests and 1GB of traffic.
The next step is Phase Router which will direct simpler requests to models running on phones in the network, or route them instead to major external providers like OpenAI and Anthropic, based on “task complexity, model capabilities, performance and cost.”
The network could eventually expand beyond smartphones to desktops, servers and GPUs, he says.
But Markus Levin, co-founder of decentralized infrastructure provider XYO, says decentralized networks may be better suited to collecting and verifying real-world data rather than running AI models.
Phones and sensors can provide localized information that centralized datasets miss, he says, but only if the data is accurate and resistant to manipulation.
“A useful decentralized AI network should be judged by whether it solves a problem customers will pay to fix, not by its token price or node count,” he says.
Coordination is the tricky part
One of the biggest challenges with mobile phone networks is coordinating the devices to provide predictable hardware, power and connectivity, in the same way data centers do.
A 2025 study tested small groups of smartphones carrying out image recognition tasks and found that clusters of phones could deliver competitive performance in certain conditions, but the results came from a controlled testing environment.
Related: Web3 companies turn to hardware with crypto-powered phones, consoles
A Google-backed project at the University of California, San Diego found that a cluster of 20 retired smartphones could handle the peak computing workload of a class of more than 75 students, with grading times faster than the university’s standard cloud setup. However, those devices were also organized in a controlled environment, not scattered across the world.
In the real world, a distributed network has to contend with phones that disconnect, overheat, run out of battery, change networks, and have varying amounts of processing power and memory.
In a blockchain network like Ethereum for example, the capacity is currently limited by how long it takes to communicate across the network, and the processing abilities of the lowest spec devices.
20 retired smartphones could handle a class of more than 75 students. Source: Google Research
Similarly, when tasks are split between several phones, slow connections or disconnected devices can throw a spanner in the works. Distributing separate, independent tasks across available phones is generally more straightforward.
Can the economics work?
Even if the technical challenges can be overcome, networks still need to make financial sense for customers and device owners alike.
Using existing smartphone hardware doesn’t incur the high capital costs of building a data center, but costs include factors like connectivity, coordination and incentives for people on the network.
When it comes to compensation, De Carli says there is “no fixed figure” because rewards for Acurast participants vary by “device uptime, hardware specifications (benchmark performance), total ACU staked and active compute demand” from developers. He says operators compete for a pool of inflation-funded rewards, rather than receiving direct payments from customers.
Phase network rewards depend on uptime, participation and customer demand.
“Phase will use a portion of its service revenue to purchase PHASE on the open market and distribute it to node operators based on their contributions to the network,” Eves says.
Running an AI model to run properly on a phone is no longer the main challenge — getting the economics to stack up while coordinating tens of thousands of phones to behave like a reliable cloud service is the real trick.

items.title: Can decentralized phone networks power the AI revolution?

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors pump out of Midterms then retrace; BTC at $79.6k

- BTC and ETH ETFs flip to inflows, breaking outflow streak
- STRC hits $100 par for the first time since May

🗳️ Democrat Sweep Pumps Crypto as Market Structure Bill Resurfaces
Bitcoin spent Tuesday night under $76,000, a seven-week low, with traders bracing for whatever a Democratic Congress meant for crypto. By Wednesday afternoon it was back above $80,800, up 4% on the day.
The easy story is that uncertainty lifted and crypto exhaled. And that could be part of it. But oil helped. WTI fell 9% to $88 a barrel, down almost 17% on the week, as Iran’s parliament speaker said voters had “said NO TO WAR.” The DOW jumped 3% on the day and Nasdaq +1.6% in what was a huge green day across markets.
James Butterfill of CoinShares put it plainly: “For Bitcoin, real yields, dollar liquidity and ETP flows still carry more weight than the elections.”
But the policy news that landed Wednesday afternoon matters more than the candles.
Eleanor Terrett reported that House Democrats are discussing expanding Maxine Waters’ Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights, originally an amendment to the CLARITY Act in 2025, into a full market structure bill next Congress. The draft would fold in Democratic CLARITY provisions that the House rejected last year, plus provisions Senate Democrats and Republicans had already agreed on before the September cloture vote that killed the bill. Three industry sources described the talks to her.
That’s a genuine surprise. Twenty-four hours ago the consensus was that market structure legislation was dead for two years. Waters is the likely incoming chair of House Financial Services, and she is apparently planning to write a bill rather than hold hearings. But the bill will have some changes.
The new proposals under discussion would give the SEC a larger role supervising crypto markets and leave the CFTC with a smaller one. The draft is expected to carry ethics provisions restricting the crypto activities of Trump and other federal officials. Those provisions are what Democrats wanted all along, and what many thought would kill any chances the bill has of getting signed.
So one of the first courses of action from this Democrat-led Congress is to enact some reasonable changes to the Clarity Act to try to get it passed in 2027. That feels like a very bullish first step.
Let the post-Trump crypto era begin…

- Crypto majors are green after a post-midterms rally; BTC +2% at $79.9k; ETH +3% at $2,390; SOL +2% at $95; HYPE -5% at $81.80; ZEC even at $1,298
- INJ (+8%), ATOM (+7%), and RAY (+6%) led top alt movers

- Coinbase said it holds more than 99% of customer assets in cold storage in a blog post responding to the Binance hack, detailing split cold-wallet keys that are never fully reassembled, rate limits on cold-to-hot transfers, and kill switches that take signing keys offline entirely
- ZachXBT named French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the alleged victim of a crypto theft now exceeding $133 million, up from the $106 million he flagged Monday

乌克兰央行反对现行加密法案：担忧货币主权，要求终审前修订

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 5 日，乌克兰国家银行 NBU 表示，不会支持当前版本的加密资产合法化与监管草案，呼吁议员在终审表决前继续修订。NBU 称支持参照欧盟 MiCA 与国际货币基金组织建议推进监管，但认为第 10225-d 号草案仍未解决其关键关切，最终文本周二晚才送达导致审议时间不足，立法过程「透明度不够」。

NBU 警告，未在发行地受充分监管的境外代币可能进入乌克兰，其中部分或充当电子货币角色，威胁货币主权与金融稳定，并可能绕开适用于本土同类资产的要求，央行希望有权评估并在必要时限制使用。市场准入方面，NBU 称曾达成初期通过竞争选出三家加密交易平台运营商的妥协，但终稿将前五年准入数量交由证券监管机构酌定，引发垄断与腐败风险担忧。按草案，乌克兰国家证券与股票市场委员会将成为主要监管者，并对存量加密资产设至 2028 年底的 5% 过渡税率，加密对加密交易明确免税。

items.content:
In brief
- Samsung Wallet launched stablecoin accounts for eligible U.S. Galaxy users, supporting USDC on Solana across about 82 million compatible devices.
- The service is built with custodian Bastion and Coinbase, and allows transfers without Samsung fees, plus bank payouts in more than 60 countries.
- Credit card top-ups carry a 4% fee, the service isn’t available in New York, and Samsung plans to explore stablecoin payments and other markets.
Samsung is putting digital dollars in the same app where its users keep their credit cards and boarding passes.
Stablecoin accounts went live in Samsung Wallet on Thursday for eligible U.S. Galaxy users, letting them buy, hold, send, and receive Circle’s USDC on the Solana blockchain without downloading a separate crypto app or managing private keys. The feature reaches about 82 million compatible Galaxy devices in the U.S., according to the announcement.
“For a decade, stablecoins have proved the technology works,” said Lily Liu, president of the Solana Foundation. “What they lacked was a way to reach the mainstream.”
SOL next move: Pump to $160 or Dump to $40?
Samsung first announced the feature on Oct. 7, when the electronics giant tapped Solana for USDC transfers. Samsung Wallet first teased plans to support the stablecoin, which is pegged to the U.S. dollar, over the summer.
The product is built with Bastion, a licensed stablecoin custodian and infrastructure provider, and Coinbase, which safeguards the USDC as Bastion’s sub-custodian through its Coinbase Prime Vault. Samsung’s disclosures stress that the account is a crypto wallet, not a bank account.
Users can send USDC to other Samsung Wallet users in the U.S. and to compatible outside crypto wallets with no Samsung transfer fee, though other providers may charge one. They can also send money to qualifying bank accounts in more than 60 countries, where recipients may receive local currency, with fees that vary by destination.
Topping up with a credit card, including through Samsung Pay, carries a 4% fee, and withdrawals to a bank account or debit card also come with a fee. New users who make a first top-up of $50 or more can receive $25 in USDC. The service requires Android 13 or later and is open to U.S. residents 18 and older, except those in New York.
"Stablecoins have the potential to make moving money around the world faster and easier, and we want Galaxy users to be able to take advantage of that without having to navigate the complexity of traditional crypto tools,” said Woncheol Chai, who leads the digital wallet team in Samsung’s mobile business. “Solana helps us bring that experience to Samsung's scale."
Samsung said it expects to explore online and in-store stablecoin payments and to expand to additional markets, subject to local regulation.

四名加密KOL遭链上调查：喊单与钱包轨迹不一致，部分涉嫌捆绑与抢跑

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 5 日，链上分析平台 Bubblemaps 发文称，近期调查了四名加密 KOL，认为其钱包动向与公开叙事并不完全一致，相关结论基于 Bubblemaps 分析与估算。关于被 Pump.Fun 上线合作的「Kimchi」，圈内曾传其在 TRUMP 上赚得约 4000 万美元，Bubblemaps 据其公开空投钱包及关联集群估算相关利润约 600 万美元，并质疑其隐瞒关联的原因。

对 Solstice，Bubblemaps 称其推广的多枚 meme 币呈现数十个新钱包同期买入、各持约 0.5% 至 1% 供应的捆绑特征，并可将公开钱包追溯至代币部署者。

对 Anglio，平台分析其 10 月约 534 条帖文后称，关联钱包在约 61% 的喊单前平均提前约 20 秒买入并很快卖出，估算获利约 13 万美元，且其本人已承认使用此类手法。

对 0xEthan，Bubblemaps 称其常在喊单后约三分钟内卖出，公开钱包与隐秘侧钱包同期买入，估算相关获利约 12.5 万美元。

items.author: frostbyte7
items.content:
--- Top Comments ---

[midnightclubbed]: This codec would have been great 27 years ago!  I suspect it wouldn't have gotten past the patent lawyers in 1999 though.  It seems cute today but the entire codec space was a patent minefield, the N64 mp3 decoder was implemented twice (once based on the reference codec, once clean) with Nintendo/Rare then paying RAD game tools to license their decoder... of which none of their code was used but they had a license from the mp3 patent holder (Fraunhofer) which then shielded Nintendo ...

[Sesse__]: I wonder if this would also be a great fit for the MAS3507D! Supposedly you can replace the program with your own in a 1-kiloword RAM (the default MP3 decoder is in ROM, and probably larger). If you can fit this codec in 1024 MIPS instructions, perhaps you can do the same in 1024 of these DSP instructions… Too bad there is seemingly zero public documentation on the format of these programs, though (and no emulator or similar).

[hxorr]: Great read, thanks! Pardon my ignorance but one thing I'm curious about, if the decoder fills almost the entire 4k RSP instruction memory (IMEM) - wouldn't that be something games need for graphics? If so, then is this still usable for say a game?

[jonas21]: In case anyone else got to the demo thinking the quality is awful -- the vocals are incomprehensible and keep cutting out -- it turns out it's like that in the original track:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i1gVxKhdGPs&t=57s

[pona-a]: Beautiful! I long wanted to write my own audio codec, this might be a nice challenge.
items.title: Obscure audio codec is a perfect fit for the N64

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
Trump’s memecoin ventures derailed CLARITY Act, Scaramucci says
The SkyBridge founder said disputes over ethics restrictions also stalled negotiations, with both sides responsible for the setback.
SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci blamed US President Donald Trump’s crypto business interests and memecoin launches for derailing the CLARITY Act, saying they cost the legislation Democratic support.
Speaking with Cointelegraph at SALT London, Scaramucci said the memecoin launches shortly before Trump’s January 2025 inauguration undermined bipartisan momentum for crypto regulation following the 2024 election.
“Singular reason,” Scaramucci told Cointelegraph when asked whether the memecoin activities were the sole reason the bill did not pass. He said Democrats who had become more receptive to crypto regulation withdrew their support following the launches.
The remarks follow the Senate’s failure to advance the CLARITY Act on Sept. 15, when a procedural motion received 49 votes in favor and 50 against, falling short of the 60 votes required. The bill, which sought to establish a federal regulatory framework for digital assets, faced disagreements over ethics provisions restricting government officials’ crypto interests.
Scaramucci says both sides share responsibility
Scaramucci also pointed to disagreements over proposed ethics restrictions, saying lawmakers sought stronger provisions that the White House opposed.
“I think it’s the business interests, the memecoins,” Scaramucci said, adding that lawmakers were “trying to put real teeth into the ethics provision” but the White House did not want to sign it.
“There’s culpability on both sides for that deal not going forward,” he said.
Related: Market participants weigh in on SEC’s proposed crypto regulations
In July, five Democratic senators called for hearings into Trump’s crypto holdings and potential conflicts of interest, citing concerns that his financial ties could influence crypto policy. House Financial Services Committee Chair French Hill also acknowledged that Trump’s crypto businesses had complicated efforts to pass legislation.
In August, consumer advocacy group Public Citizen estimated that investors incurred at least $4.7 billion in largely unrealized losses across Trump-related crypto ventures, including $3.2 billion associated with the Official Trump (TRUMP) memecoin. The group said Trump earned $635 million in memecoin licensing fees in 2025, citing his financial disclosure.
Despite the legislative setback, Scaramucci said the SEC’s approach under Chair Paul Atkins could help tokenization reach “escape velocity,” with enough adoption to make it difficult for a future SEC chair to stop or slow the industry.
He said it was too early to know whether adoption would reach that point before the next administration.

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
Elon Musk funneled $474 million into Tuesday’s US midterms, and based on polling estimates after a definitive Democratic sweep, approximately 98% of that money went to losing candidates.
A trace of Musk’s midterm donations by Wired estimated even higher: 99% to losers.
Even worse, Musk ended up losing an additional $33 billion of personal net worth within 24 hours of polls closing, as spooked investors in Tesla and SpaceX sold down shares in fear of political tides turning after the blue wave.
Most of Musk’s donations went to Republican super PACs, political action committees that can raise unlimited amounts of money.
Federal filings trace Musk’s money through three main pipes. His own America PAC collected roughly $216 million, the Senate Leadership Fund took $168 million, and the Congressional Leadership Fund, which backs House Republicans, took $30 million.
Musk steered at least $225 million into Texas, by OpenSecrets’ count, including Ken Paxton’s doomed campaign for Senator. Paxton lost to Democrat James Talarico by a double-digit margin in a surprising upset for the historically conservative state.
Ad-tracking firm AdImpact called Tuesday’s Texas Senate seat contest the costliest Senate race on record for political advertising, with $573 million in spending and reservations through October 30.
Musk was the largest single donor to that race, and his candidate lost.
Musk $33 billion poorer after midterms
Both of Musk’s publicly traded companies, Tesla and SpaceX, sank in Wednesday’s trading session as news of Musk’s political losses disseminated.
Tesla fell more than 5% in early trading before closing 3.3% lower than Tuesday’s close. SpaceX, public only since June, dropped more than 7% premarket and closed 3.8% lower than Tuesday.
Bloomberg’s Billionaires Index put his one-day net worth decline at $33.5 billion, a 3.7% drop to $865 billion, even while the broader market rallied.
XTB research director Kathleen Brooks explained, “There is now a political risk premium attached to both Tesla and SpaceX that could weigh on their share prices.”
Read more: Justin Sun takes on Elon Musk in race to be Trump’s top donor
Musk responded by posting, “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” a reference to xAI and Grok’s AI infrastructure that might become threatened in Texas.
Then he added, “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time.”
In addition, he quietly deleted his election day plea to vote Republican.
This cycle, The Atlantic estimated Musk’s giving at about a quarter of all donations Republicans received for this week’s midterm campaigns.

items.content: In brief - Binance has removed all API keys linked to SignalPlus after the third-party crypto options trading platform reported a potential security issue. - The exchange said its own systems are unaffected and user funds are safe, and urged SignalPlus users to check their positions and open orders. - The move comes a week after Binance lost about $6.3 billion in a hack that the FBI has attributed to North Korea. Binance has removed all API keys linked to SignalPlus, a third-party crypto trading platform, after SignalPlus reported a "potential security issue," the exchange said on Thursday. "Binance's own systems are unaffected. User funds remain safe," the exchange said, describing the move as an "immediate precautionary measure." Following a potential security issue reported by third-party platform SignalPlus, we have proactively removed all API keys linked to SignalPlus as an immediate precautionary measure. Binance's own systems are unaffected. User funds remain safe. If you used SignalPlus, please… pic.twitter.com/0HYYkTAW2p — Binance (@binance) November 5, 2026 API keys let third-party apps and trading tools connect to a user's exchange account and place trades on their behalf. Removing them cuts off that connection, meaning any automated strategies running on Binance through SignalPlus will stop until users set up new keys. Binance urged SignalPlus users to log into their accounts directly to review their positions and open orders. It recommended that they wait until SignalPlus confirms the issue is fully resolved before reconnecting, and that they always enable IP whitelisting, which restricts an API key to approved internet addresses. The exchange also called on all third-party platforms integrated with Binance to review their security controls, watch for unusual activity and contact it immediately if they spot any concerns. SignalPlus, a Hong Kong-based platform that provides trading tools for crypto options and derivatives, connects to several exchanges, including Binance. Binance's hack and recovery The incident comes a week after Binance was hit by the largest hack in crypto history, in which attackers drained about $6.4 billion from its hot wallets on October 29. The FBI has attributed the theft to North Korean hackers it calls TraderTraitor, a claim Pyongyang has denied. Binance has said the attack began when a fake recruiter persuaded one of its engineers to download a malware-laced coding assignment, and that the attackers then used stolen credentials to reach an internal wallet signing service. Binance said on Wednesday that it has replenished about 98% of the stolen assets from its own funds, and is still buying the rest, mostly less liquid tokens, through market and over-the-counter channels. It has also taken a new proof-of-reserves snapshot covering 44 tokens, up from 10, which users will be able to verify once its zero-knowledge proof is generated in about 50 to 60 hours. The exchange is still restoring services. On Thursday, it began reopening withdrawals for more assets in phases, prioritizing tokens based on user demand over the past week. Deposits remain open. BlockBeats 消息，11 月 5 日，马来西亚国家新闻社 Bernama 报道称，马六甲警方昨日在 Kota Shahbandar 一处住宅突袭，逮捕 13 名外籍嫌疑人，捣毁涉及「杀猪盘」及虚构加密货币交易平台的网络诈骗团伙，逮捕 13 名外籍嫌疑人。

马六甲中央警区主任 Halim Abas 称，团伙通过 Telegram、QQ 及 Soul 等应用以甜言蜜语诱骗中国籍受害者，并要求对方在号称高回报的加密交易中转账。初步调查显示，成员去年 2 月至 9 月间持旅游签证自菲律宾、台湾地区、老挝及中国等地乘机入境，约三个月前开始在该处作业。警方扣押 12 台笔记本电脑、1 台台式机、26 部手机及一台路由器，估值约 5 万令吉，嫌疑人已被还押至 11 月 8 日协助调查，受害者总损失仍在核实中。

--- Top Comments ---

[mpyne]: OK, I think I see what’s going on with this, in this configuration. The goal from an attacker’s perspective is to get this to be true: `$ret = crypt($pw, $hash); $ret == $hash` when called by OpenSSH’s sshd. This is how sshd validates that the user logging in knew the account password. The `$hash` is the “settings” to the crypt call and will normally look like “$6$--gibberish” for users with passwords set, but could look like “*” or “!” for users not intended to be able to login. The bug is f...

[BoppreH]: In-band signaling[1] strikes again. * should not have been used as special value, neither for "no password" in /etc/passwd  nor  "error while hashing the password" in crypt. I'm afraid we'll find many more of these abuses, specially in string manipulations. The null was ok, an exception (or equivalent) better, and Result<T> (or equivalent) best. [1]  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In-band_signaling#Computer_dat...

[dabinat]: This is why I don’t fully buy the argument that software that’s been around for a long time is more secure and reliable because it’s been battle-tested. There’s been a lot of time for cruft to accumulate until no-one can ever fix it because everyone is expecting it to function in the broken manner it’s always functioned. And some of the more obscure configuration options get a lot less scrutiny.

[amluto]: The whole story is a bit worse than this.  Musl  already worked around this type of failure .  See the second-to-last line here:  https://git.musl-libc.org/cgit/musl/tree/src/crypt/crypt_des...  (hey, this workaround is wrong if the salt is "x"!) but they forgot to work around it here:  https://git.musl-libc.org/cgit/musl/tree/src/crypt/crypt_sha...  The vulnerable path in musl is only a little bit vulne...

[aljgz]: My general rule of thumb is: "no magic strings". This is much easier to implement in higher-level languages and when writing application/web code than system programming. Don't return empty string/asterisk/anything else. Instead, return a failure value. When absolutely needed, choose the magic string with more caution: One string showing the SHA-256 of a non-existing hash? It's a good idea for it to be a valid hash. Now we have a new risk: if it's broke...

GitBook安全事件复盘：攻击指向Trade.xyz，SSO漏洞致生产环境失陷

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 5 日，GitBook 发布 11 月 2 日安全事件复盘称，攻击者利用其单点登录流程漏洞伪造员工登录会话，进而查询组织内配置不当的 GitHub App 认证信息，进入内部代码仓库并拿到 Cloudflare API 密钥，最终借服务账户获得完整生产环境权限。GitBook 在数小时内禁用相关内部服务账户切断攻击，平台因此下线约 16 小时，并于 11 月 3 日 11:56 UTC 全面恢复。攻击者在生产环境累计约停留 3 小时 25 分钟，GitBook 已轮换全部基础设施与托管客户密钥并作废 API 令牌。

GitBook 表示，现有迹象显示攻击针对单一客户而非平台整体，未发现其他客户内容被篡改，但因攻击者可触及平台内客户数据，已按全部客户数据均可能暴露处理，涉及 API 令牌、集成密钥、会话签名密钥、助手问答记录及已授权仓库的 GitHub、GitLab 应用权限等，账单信息、密码与 IP 地址未受影响。GitBook 称攻击推进速度与精度高度依赖自动化与 AI。慢雾首席信息安全官 23pds 转发该复盘称，被点名目标即为 Trade.xyz。Trade.xyz 此前表示，文档异常来自 GitBook 基础设施遭入侵，自身基础设施未见被攻破迹象，并将在数日内迁离 GitBook。

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- A Canadian man has been extradited to the U.S. on charges of hacking university computers to steal login credentials and secretly mine cryptocurrency.
- Prosecutors say Ryan James Roach and Mathiew James Stubbings targeted educational institutions with supercomputers in four states between 2016 and 2019.
- The case comes as Google warns that hackers are moving from cryptojacking to hijacking access to AI models, a practice known as LLMjacking.
A Canadian man has been extradited to the United States to face charges that he helped hack into university computers to steal login credentials and secretly mine cryptocurrency, the Justice Department said on Tuesday.
A federal grand jury in the Western District of New York indicted Ryan James Roach, 35, of Saskatchewan, and Mathiew James Stubbings, 41, of Ontario, on charges of conspiracy to obtain information from and damage a protected computer, obtaining information from a protected computer, and intentionally damaging a protected computer. The charges carry a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.
Canadian man extradited to the U.S. for his role in computer hacking scheme targeting universities... @FBIBuffalo @USDOJ_Intl https://t.co/vY8IacXdZZ pic.twitter.com/NsSZ5BIkIf
— WDNYnews (@WDNYnews) November 4, 2026
Between June 2016 and December 2019, the pair targeted U.S. educational institutions with supercomputers, researching security weaknesses in their networks before breaking in, according to the indictment. Once inside, they allegedly deployed malware, stole login credentials and forced the victims' computers to mine cryptocurrency for their own benefit.
Victims included institutions in New York, Tennessee, North Carolina and Massachusetts, among them a university in the Western District of New York, prosecutors said. The pair allegedly used virtual private servers in several countries, registered under false names, to send malware and mining software to victim computers and store stolen credentials, and routed attacks through computers compromised at other victims to hide their identities.
Roach was extradited from Canada on October 28 and arraigned in Rochester, New York, where he was held pending a detention hearing. Extradition proceedings against Stubbings are continuing in Canada.
From cryptojacking to LLMjacking
The scheme is a form of cryptojacking, in which attackers use other people's computers to mine crypto while the victims bear the electricity costs and slower performance. The Justice Department did not say which cryptocurrency the pair allegedly mined.
Privacy coin Monero has long been a favorite for such schemes because it can be mined on ordinary hardware. In August, the Dutch national cyber agency warned that attackers were exploiting a flaw in Apple's macOS Screen Sharing feature to plant Monero miners on Macs.
But hackers looking to profit from stolen computing power may be turning elsewhere. In a report published Monday, Google's Threat Intelligence Group said it expects attackers to "increasingly prioritize LLMJacking over traditional resource theft like cryptojacking," hijacking companies' access to AI models and passing on the bills.
Unlike the gradual drain of cryptojacking, LLMjacking can run up huge cloud charges within hours, Google said. In incidents investigated by its Mandiant unit this year, fraudulent charges topped $100,000 in a single day, and some organizations racked up $1 million before access was cut off. Attackers are reselling stolen access through underground services that Google calls "LLM Mixers."

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
Thailand to block Bitget in December over unlicensed crypto trading
Thailand’s SEC filed a criminal complaint against Bitget’s operator, with access to its website and app set to be blocked from Dec. 5.
Thailand’s securities regulator has filed a criminal complaint against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, for allegedly operating without a license.
Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said Thursday that it had notified the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society to block access to Bitget from Dec. 5. The restriction will cover Bitget’s website, other associated domains and its mobile app.
The regulator advised users to take action regarding assets held on the platform before the deadline.
The complaint follows Bitget’s Oct. 20 announcement of plans to acquire a licensed Thai crypto exchange.
SEC cites Thai language promotions and trading fees
According to the SEC, Bitget offered crypto trading services between 2022 and 2025, charged trading fees and promoted its services in Thai through its websites and social media channels. The regulator said these activities violated Thailand’s digital asset business licensing requirements.
The complaint also names Kritsana Kritsananuwat, whom the SEC accused of helping promote Bitget through Facebook and YouTube. The watchdog previously filed a criminal complaint against him in March 2025 over allegations that he helped promote OKX’s unlicensed exchange activities.
Cointelegraph attempted to contact Kritsananuwat through a phone number listed for advertising inquiries in a video on his YouTube channel but was unable to reach him.
Thailand introduced licensing requirements for digital asset businesses in 2018 and tightened the rules in April 2025 to cover foreign platforms targeting Thai users. Changes to a separate cybercrime law also made it easier for the ministry to block access to unlicensed platforms.
Related: Thailand SEC says several companies eye crypto ETFs, none has applied
The regulator filed the complaint with Thailand’s Economic Crime Suppression Division for investigation. Prosecutors will decide whether to bring charges, while courts will determine criminal liability.
Bitget did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s request for comment.
Bitget pursued licensed Thai presence ahead of SEC complaint
Bitget announced plans on Oct. 20 to acquire GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics, a locally licensed crypto exchange and brokerage, through BTGT Management (Thailand), a company in which Bitget said it held an interest.
The proposed acquisition remained subject to regulatory approval and other conditions at the time of the disclosure. Bitget said it intended to introduce its trading platform to Thai users after completing the transaction and obtaining approval for the change of control.
“Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said at the time.

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
Claude Code修复后台子Agent「偷吃额度」：状态更新成本降低99%

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 修复了 Claude Code 一项浪费额度的问题。此前，开发者发现，后台子 Agent 即使没有执行新任务，也会因为不断汇报进度而消耗大量 Token。

Claude Code 可以让多个子 Agent 在后台同时工作，比如查代码、修 Bug、运行测试。为了显示任务进展，每个子 Agent 约每 30 秒更新一次状态。

问题在于，此前每次更新状态，模型都要重新读取整个对话记录，哪怕最终只生成几个字。任务运行越久，重复消耗的 Token 就越多。

10 月底，有开发者发现，团队一周内约 16.4% 的模型费用花在了这些状态更新上。Anthropic 工程师随后确认了这一机制，但表示这属于较极端的案例。

现在，Claude Code 改用更便宜的 Haiku 5.5，根据简短笔记生成状态提示，不再反复读取完整对话。官方称，单次状态更新成本降低约 99%，使用后台子 Agent 的会话整体节省约 5% 的额度，相当于同样额度能多发约 6% 的请求。

这项优化仅针对 Claude Code 命令行版本，不涉及桌面应用。目前已向大部分 Pro、Max、Ultra 用户及全部 Team、Enterprise 用户开放，需更新至 v2.1.316 或更高版本。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/375718

矿企Riot与Anthropic签署280亿美元AI数据中心协议，或向其支付12%年利息

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 5 日，比特币矿企 Riot Platforms 与 Anthropic 签署了一项为期 15 年、总额约 280 亿美元的协议，将为 Anthropic 在美国得克萨斯州 Corsicana 园区提供 910 兆瓦数据中心容量，全部投运后预计年均租金收入约 18 亿美元。

不过，项目建设成本预计高达 55 亿美元，其中约 18 亿美元用于 Riot 自身的场地及电力基础设施建设，最高 36 亿美元用于补偿 Anthropic 的数据中心设施建设成本。Riot 计划通过债务融资覆盖项目成本的 80% 至 90%，自身预计投入约 5 亿至 11 亿美元，融资工作计划于 2027 年启动。

值得注意的是，根据 Riot 提交的季度文件，Anthropic 可通过抵扣未来租金收回符合条件的设施建设成本，并获得 12% 的年利息。这意味着 Riot 可能需要在租金之外，承担数十亿美元建设成本对应的利息支出。

Riot 此前已持续出售比特币为数据中心转型融资。2026 年前九个月，该公司累计出售 20,264 枚 BTC，套现约 15 亿美元。截至 9 月底，其仅剩 2,418 枚 BTC，并预计未来将继续出售几乎全部新开采的比特币。项目首批数据中心容量预计于 2027 年 6 月交付。

Atmee v2发布：一张照片生成AI角色，能实时聊天、做动作，连周围环境都能生成

动察 Beating AI 快讯，AI 初创公司 Atmanity 发布实时视频模型 Atmee v2。只需一张照片和 10 秒录音，就能生成一个可以面对面聊天的 AI 角色。它能根据对话内容实时生成表情、手势和身体动作，还能与周围环境互动。

官方演示中，一个卡通角色会主动凑近镜头、逗用户笑，两名 AI 主持人无需预设台词就能实时对谈。团队还用一条小巷的照片，让模型连续生成可控制的街景，不过画面仍会出现扭曲。

为了让角色自然互动，团队训练了两套模型。一套负责判断角色何时说话、倾听，以及该做什么动作；另一套负责实时生成视频画面。官方称，一张 GPU 就能运行整套系统。

Atmanity 创始人余正平此前创办过 AR 导航公司 Phiar，2022 年被谷歌收购。此后他再次创业，花了两年研究实时视频 AI，希望让人们像视频通话一样直接与 AI 交流。

Atmee v2 也能像 Seedance 2.5、Wan 3.0 一样生成普通视频。在以人物为主的视频生成任务中，速度最高快 50 倍，成本降低 10 至 100 倍。

目前 Atmee v2 还需要申请邀请码，Beta 版及 API 即将推出。
